aspects.says: Key fields must be echoed unchanged by the host, and in 2.1.7 the plain key element must come first.
aspects.reason: configuration order is observed only by reading the computed key, which the lesson shows; a practice would only retype the configuration

aspects.says: A response finds its request because both produce the same key; what differs between them (the response digit, the repeat digit) is left out.
basis: section:12.2 A Response Finds Its Request Through a Key

aspects.says: An answer that arrives after its request gave up has nobody waiting and goes to the request listeners or the unhandled queue.
basis: section:12.2.1 A Late Answer Has Nobody to Go To

aspects.says: Only one request per key can wait, so the sender of a link must number its own messages; per-terminal or relayed STANs collide.
basis: section:12.3 Only One Request per Key Can Wait
section:12.3.1 Spot the Problem: The Gateway at Lunchtime

aspects.says: A reversal is a new message with its own STAN that points at the original through field 90.
basis: section:12.6 A Reversal Points Back at the Original

aspects.says: With no answer the outcome is unknown: purchases are reversed and never resent, advices are repeated, network messages need nothing, and what never went out needs nothing.
basis: section:12.5 No Answer Means You Don't Know

aspects.says: A store-and-forward queue keeps a message stored while it is sent, repeats it only after a real attempt, keeps its place, and counts any answer as delivery.
basis: section:12.7 A Reversal Must Outlive the Process and Wait Its Turn

aspects.says: A message the host never answers is parked after the allowed attempts, with the count stored alongside it, so it neither blocks the line nor gets deleted.
basis: section:12.7 A Reversal Must Outlive the Process and Wait Its Turn

aspects.says: Each timeout guards a different wait: servers need a read timeout, echoes must come more often than it fires, and the request timeout ends before the caller gives up.
basis: section:12.4 Every Timeout Guards a Different Wait
